planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade, allowing generous room for its eventual size.

directions: Big-leaf daphniphyllum is an evergreen shrub or small tree from Japan, Taiwan, and parts of China, grown for its exceptionally large, glossy, leathery leaves carried on reddish petioles, which give it a bolder, more tropical look than its smaller-leaved relative D. macropodum. Like other daphniphyllums it is dioecious, with inconspicuous spring flowers followed by small blue-black drupes on female plants growing near a male pollinator. It tolerates deep shade better than almost any other broadleaf evergreen, making it valuable as a substantial specimen or screening plant beneath high tree canopy. Give it humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil and protection from harsh winter wind at the cold end of its range.

planting.note: Plant in filtered woodland shade in consistently moist, humus-rich soil, reserving it for the milder, humid-winter end of its hardiness range.

directions: Glaucous daphniphyllum is a smaller, more tender relative of the better-known D. macropodum, native to subtropical forests of Taiwan and southern China, and prized by shade-garden collectors for the blue-gray cast on the undersides of its glossy evergreen leaves. Like other daphniphyllums it bears inconspicuous flowers in spring, with small dark fruit forming on female plants pollinated by a nearby male. It prefers filtered woodland shade and consistently moist, humus-rich soil, and is best suited to mild, humid winters rather than hard freezes. Its smaller stature compared to other daphniphyllums makes it a useful choice where space beneath a shade canopy is limited.

planting.note: Site in the dappled light of a woodland understory with cool, consistently moist, humus-rich soil, avoiding hot, dry, or reflected-heat exposures.

directions: Wheel tree is a slow-growing evergreen shrub or small tree native to the forests of Japan, Taiwan, and Korea, named for its unusual spring flowers, which lack petals but display their green stamens arranged in a distinctive wheel-like ring. Its glossy, spirally arranged leaves and tiered branching give it year-round structural interest even without its curious flowers. It thrives in the dappled light of a woodland understory, where its roots stay cool and moist, and resents hot, dry exposure or reflected heat. Though ultimately capable of reaching tree size over many decades, it is slow enough to serve for years as a refined large shrub in a shaded border.

planting.note: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, where it tolerates shearing into a dense hedge or background planting.

directions: Chinese eurya is a dense, small-leaved evergreen shrub from East Asia, long used in Chinese and Japanese gardens as a shade-tolerant hedge or background plant and as a favored subject for bonsai because of its fine, compact foliage. Its tiny spring flowers are inconspicuous and best appreciated up close, giving way to small dark berries on female plants later in the season. It takes shearing well and holds a tidy, dense habit even in low light beneath trees or alongside taller shrubs, where it is valued more for year-round structure than for seasonal display. Provide humus-rich, well-drained soil and even moisture, since it does not tolerate prolonged drought.

planting.note: Site in a sheltered, partially shaded spot with moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil and protection from harsh winter wind.

directions: Yunnan osmanthus is one of the larger-growing members of its genus, a vigorous evergreen shrub or small tree native to mountain forests of Yunnan, China, where it grows as an understory plant beneath taller canopy trees. Its leathery, toothed leaves are larger and coarser than those of the familiar sweet olive, and in late winter to early spring it carries clusters of small, fragrant white flowers along the stems. Grown mainly by collectors and specialty gardens outside its native range, it rewards a partially shaded, sheltered site with steady, if unhurried, growth into a substantial background or screening plant. Moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil suits it best, with protection from harsh winter wind at the cooler edge of its hardiness range.

planting.note: Plant in cool, consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade, sheltered from drying winds, as a woodland-border evergreen.

directions: Small-flowered anise tree is an evergreen shrub from the mountain forests of southern China, grown for its glossy, aromatic foliage and tidy, upright habit rather than for conspicuous bloom, since its small flowers are pale and easily overlooked among the leaves. Like its showier relatives in the genus, its leaves release a spicy anise-like fragrance when bruised, and the whole plant works well as an evergreen component of a shaded woodland border. It prefers the same cool, moist, humus-rich conditions as other understory Illicium species and resists deer better than many broadleaf evergreens. Give it shelter from drying winds and consistent soil moisture, especially while young.

planting.note: Plant a male and female together in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in deep to partial shade to ensure berry set on female plants.

directions: Himalayan skimmia is an evergreen shrub native to the understory of Himalayan forests from Pakistan through Nepal to southwestern China, grown for its leathery, pointed leaves that release a musky, laurel-like scent when crushed. Like other skimmias it is typically dioecious, with small, fragrant flower clusters in spring followed by red to blackish berries on female plants grown near a male pollinator. It is well suited to deep, dry shade beneath trees where few other broadleaf evergreens perform, though it still benefits from humus-rich soil and occasional watering during drought. Its compact, mounding habit makes it useful as underplanting or low structure in a woodland garden.
